subject: Re: [rstan] Rename extract method because it conflicts with `tidyr::extract` (#118)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [rstan] Rename extract method because it conflicts with `tidyr::extract` (#118)
parts:
[cc-ing stan-users]

Thanks. We've known about some pending conflicts for
a while now.

The right thing to do from a programming point of view
is use namespaces. R's defaults are very badly behaved
from a conventional programming point of view, because
they load all the namespaces into the top level.

I don't believe namespaces are widely known among R
programmers. Hadley has a tutorial:

http://r-pkgs.had.co.nz/namespace.html

In short, you should be able to use tidyr::extract for the
tidy version and rstan::extract for the Stan version.

- Bob

> On Feb 25, 2015, at 9:39 AM, Juan Sebastián Casallas <notifi...@github.com> wrote:
>
> I wanted to point out that there is another name clash with magrittr::extract. magrittr which provides the pipe operator (%>%) in R is also becoming very popular (and is also authored by Hadley Wickham) and I've come across this problem a couple of times, my current solution is to load all the packages in the correct order (i.e. library(magrittr);library(rstan) at the top of my scripts to avoid weird errors.
>
> Interestingly, magrittr's x %>% extract(1) is equivalent to x[1], and x %>% extract2(1) is equivalent to x[[1]] which is close to what you guys were discussing!
>
> —
